title: How Sure Is the Gripper: Carrying the Doubt in the Joints Through the Arm to the Tool

questions.question: The joints are known to 0.02 rad. Is the tool known to the same accuracy?
options: No: an angle error becomes a length error through the Jacobian, which depends on the pose, and not equally in x and y
questions.explanation: With the elbow at 90 degrees the tool's variances were 0.13 and 0.04 for joint spreads of 0.2 and 0.3.

questions.question: What is the covariance of the tool, given the covariance C of the joints and the Jacobian J?
options: J C J transposed: the tool moves by J times the joint error
questions.explanation: The formula is exact for small errors and a linear approximation otherwise.

questions.question: How well does the formula agree with 20000 random trials for joint spreads of 0.01 and 0.3 rad?
options: Well then badly: 5.02e-05 against 5.03e-05, then 4.52e-02 against 4.00e-02, because the arm's sines and cosines show for large errors
questions.explanation: For large errors use the trials themselves.

questions.question: The 95 percent ellipse of the propagated doubt held what share of 20000 trials?
Near a straight arm, what happens to the doubt at the tool?
options: It is nearly all along one direction: with the elbow at 0.05 rad the spread was 19.69 mm along and 0.20 across, a ratio of 97
questions.explanation: The Jacobian loses a direction at the singularity of lesson 13-04.

questions.question: Why is a single accuracy number for the tool not enough?
options: It hides the shape: the tool may be known to a fraction of a millimetre across the arm and ten times worse along it, and a task needs the direction it works in
questions.explanation: Report the ellipse and its axes.
